markdown_report:
The best initial direction remains a controlled recent-history dependence probe for the supplied HSTU, preserving its diagnostic interface and validation HR@10 as the sole model-selection criterion. Its ability to guide improvements is an untested hypothesis.

**Starting-point insights.** (1) Existing sampled margins measure discrimination, not useful next-choice relevance. Unobserved candidates are not verified dislikes. (2) Feedback distinguishes recent specific interests from broad historical associations. Perturbations measure model dependence, not causal intent. (3) Compatibility and fulfilled needs are often unobserved. Missing evidence must remain unknown.

**Related-work insights.** (1) HSTU uses gated, non-softmax aggregation [1]. Deletion can change readout content, positional distances, and implementation-dependent normalization. (2) Shuffling studies motivate separating last-item dependence from earlier-order dependence [2]. Training-only sensitivity can reflect memorization. (3) Betello et al. delete training interactions and retrain SASRec/GRU4Rec [3]. Their results do not validate frozen-HSTU interventions; ranking stability also does not establish quality.

The framework has three directions:

| Direction | Existing evidence | Proposed extension | Interpretation limit |
|---|---|---|---|
| Ranking separation | Positive–negative margins | Fixed-candidate paired ranks | Sample-dependent discrimination |
| Temporal dependence | Intact histories | Controlled deletion and shuffling | Sensitivity, not causal intent |
| Evidence quality | Qualitative feedback | Source-backed attributes and unknowns | Coverage, not verified demand |

Three atomic ideas merit consideration. Scores are originality/potential/code difficulty, each 0–10; higher difficulty means harder implementation.

- **Controlled recent-history probe: 5/7/5.** Originality: combines established controls within HSTU; introduces no new estimator. Potential: generates testable hypotheses; sensitivity may not predict validation gains. Difficulty: reuses scoring hooks; temporal alignment and position-preserving controls require care. [1–3]
- **Explicit-attribute evidence audit: 4/6/5.** Originality: adapts conservative extraction; extraction itself is established. Potential: separates conflicts from unknowns; sparse descriptions limit coverage. Difficulty: local rules are accessible; auditing identifiers and units takes effort. [4]
- **Jointly learned recent-context gate: 4/7/6.** Originality: adds a recent-context residual within one HSTU; gating is familiar. Potential: could adapt current interests; may amplify noisy recency shortcuts. Difficulty: standard operations suffice; retraining and predictor synchronization consume budget. [1,3]

At 0% progress, select the first idea. Freeze one checkpoint/category; cache training-prefix targets and, where accessible, validation cases separately. Compare intact histories, recent deletions, count-matched random/older deletions, and repeated prefix shuffles preserving the latest item. Add matched deletions preserving that item. Keep padded width, candidates, prediction time and final-nonpadding readout fixed. Compare compacted versus coordinate-preserving removal only when the backbone supports explicit masking.

Report paired rank, reciprocal-rank and HR@10 changes; top-10 overlap means intersection size/10. Optional FRBO must specify k and p [3]. Stratify by category/history length; bootstrap paired users within category and recompute the macro-average. Record ties, counts, seeds and unavailable measurements as null. Training-versus-validation differences can flag memorization, without proving it. Keep full-catalog qualitative cases separate from sampled ranking. These diagnostics motivate single-model experiments; only the unchanged host evaluator can establish validation gains.

idea.description: Add controlled, paired recent-history sensitivity diagnostics to the corrected HSTU through the existing DiagnosisProbe interface. Keep one independently trained checkpoint per category and leave production prediction unchanged. Separate frozen-model input sensitivity from robustness measured after retraining.
idea.motivation: The feedback suggests insufficient discrimination between broad historical relatedness and a specific current interest. Existing embedding and margin probes cannot distinguish recent-history dependence, last-item dependence, sensitivity to losing any comparable amount of information, or memorized sequence patterns. Controlled probes can generate hypotheses, but their usefulness must subsequently be assessed against actual host validation HR@10 changes.
idea.implementation_notes:
Retain DiagnosisProbe(view, device), run_full_diagnosis(train_loader), and diagnosis_interpreter_prompt(raw_diagnosis), returning metrics and metric_definitions. Preserve existing embedding-collapse and sampled-margin metrics; unavailable category breakdowns remain empty. Use view.model as the actual module and preserve item_emb, log2feats(sequence), predict_score(features, items), user_train, meta_data, and review_data. Restore the original train/eval state after probing, use no_grad, disable dropout, and recompute features without stale caches.

Build a deterministic training panel from observed training histories only: select up to 200 eligible users/category with a local seed-42 generator, then use each selected user's final training interaction as a diagnostic target and its preceding interactions as the prefix. Require at least four visible prefix events; record exclusions and history truncation. These targets were available during fitting, so label them in-sample diagnostics. Where existing host-accessible validation cases and candidates are available, evaluate them as a separate held-out panel; do not modify the evaluator, access test data, or silently reconstruct supposedly identical host candidates. If validation inputs are unavailable, return null with a reason. Never train on diagnostic validation targets.

Cache user IDs, target IDs, visible histories, candidate IDs and RNG seeds. Use the target plus 99 unique negatives, with the target always excluded from negatives. Apply the benchmark's observed-item exclusion rule consistently using only information allowed at that prediction point; preserve a legitimate repeated target even when it also occurs in the prefix. If fewer than 99 eligible negatives exist, report the case as ineligible rather than changing candidate count. Freeze candidates across every intervention; do not resample based on the perturbed prefix. Sampled ranks remain subject to sampling bias and do not substitute for full-catalog qualitative recommendations.

Inspect the supplied HSTU's actual masking, position bias, normalization and timestamp handling before enabling architecture-specific controls. Keep padded width L fixed. Let n be the visible prefix length and k=min(max(1,floor(n/4)),n-2). Compare deletion of the latest k events with deletion of k uniformly sampled positions and k oldest events. This first comparison includes changing the readout token. Separately compare deletion of the k events immediately before the latest event with random deletion of k nonfinal positions and oldest-event deletion, preserving the latest token in all three conditions. Repeat stochastic controls five times. Include five prefix shuffles that preserve the latest item; an additional full shuffle can quantify the combined effect of moving that item. Describe these as different interventions, not interchangeable recency estimates.

All compacted variants retain left padding and use the greatest nonpadding index, never count-1. Compaction changes relative positions. If the backbone explicitly supports retained coordinates and event masks, add coordinate-preserving removal with the same deletion sets and surviving timestamps. Do not approximate that control by inserting ordinary padding tokens into unsupported interior positions; report it unavailable instead. Keep prediction time fixed. If temporal bias exists, shuffle item identities across fixed timestamp slots as the primary ordering probe; permuting complete item–timestamp pairs is a separate, potentially nonchronological intervention. If the current sequence-only ModelView cannot express timestamps or retained coordinates, document the limitation without changing its public signatures or claiming those confounds were controlled.

Compute per-condition target rank, reciprocal rank, and diagnostic HR@10, then paired changes relative to intact histories. Preserve host tie handling for official scores. For diagnostics report tied-target frequency and optimistic/pessimistic bounds: optimistic rank=1+number of competitors strictly above the target; pessimistic rank=1+number greater than or equal to it. Use a deterministic item-ID tie break for list overlap. Top-10 overlap=|A intersection B|/10 for unique-item lists, not Jaccard. Optional FRBO@10 uses p=0.9 and [(1-p)/(1-p^10)] times sum over d=1..10 of p^(d-1)*|A[:d] intersection B[:d]|/d; distinguish it from extrapolated RBO. Identity interventions must reproduce original scores/ranks; identical and disjoint lists must have overlap/FRBO 1 and 0, respectively.

Average randomized repetitions within each example and examples within user before summarizing categories. Report history-length strata 4–9, 10–19, 20–49 and 50+, eligible users/examples, and missingness. Use 2,000 seed-42 paired bootstrap replicates, sampling users with replacement independently within each category and retaining each sampled user's complete paired observations. Recompute the equal-weight four-category macro-average and report a percentile 95% interval; if any category has no eligible cases, the four-category macro is unavailable. Intervals describe user-sampling uncertainty conditional on the checkpoint and cached candidates, not training uncertainty or confidence in causal intent.

Do not infer unavailable categories, ratings, reviews, compatibility, fulfilled needs, or simulator traits. Preserve the twenty real training-user qualitative cases, five/category, and keep their full-catalog feedback separate from sampled diagnostic metrics. Track unknown evidence separately from explicit mismatch. Repeated validation-guided changes can overfit the validation set; predeclare controls, record every authorized trial, and assess any association between diagnostic changes and validation gains as exploratory. A recent-context gate should be considered only after diagnosis and trained jointly within the sole HSTU, with no independently fitted residual scores or fusion.

Keep all four dataset routes, DATA_DIR=os.environ['GAGC_DATA_DIR'], trial-local artifacts, preprocessing seed 0, training seed 42, maximum 200 epochs, and 200 batches per epoch. Use one GPU and account for probe/retraining costs within the shared 43,200 GPU-second budget. No extra fitting is required for this idea. Any later architecture change must update the embedded predictor writer and preserve checkpoint compatibility. The unchanged host's macro validation HR@10 remains the sole selection metric; no improvement has yet been measured.
idea.pseudocode:
save model.training
model.eval()
with no_grad():
    inspect implemented HSTU mask/position/time behavior
    panels = cache_training_panel(seed=42, max_users_per_category=200)
    add separate validation panel only if existing permitted cases are accessible
    for panel, category, user, history, target, candidates in panels:
        require fixed unique candidates and at least 4 visible prefix events
        baseline = score_fresh(history, candidates, width=L, readout=last_nonpadding)
        verify identity intervention reproduces baseline
        k = min(max(1, len(history)//4), len(history)-2)
        deletion_sets = recent_k, oldest_k
        deletion_sets += five random_k sets
        deletion_sets += prefinal_k and five random_nonfinal_k sets
        variants = fixed_width_compacted_deletions(deletion_sets)
        variants += five prefix_shuffles_keep_last
        variants += separately labeled full_shuffles
        if explicit coordinate/mask support exists:
            variants += coordinate_preserving_deletions(deletion_sets)
        else:
            record unsupported control as null with reason
        for variant in variants:
            preserve supported timestamp semantics and prediction time
            scores = score_fresh(variant, candidates, width=L, readout=last_nonpadding)
            record paired rank/RR/HR10 changes, tie bounds, overlap10
            optionally record FRBO10(p=0.9)
    average random repetitions, then examples within each user
    summarize separately by panel, category and history-length stratum
    paired_bootstrap_users_within_category(seed=42, replicates=2000)
    recompute four-category macro and percentile 95% interval per replicate
restore model.training
return {'metrics': metrics, 'metric_definitions': definitions}

originality.positive: Combines matched deletion, last-item-preserving shuffles, and HSTU-aware controls within the required diagnostic contract.
originality.negative: Perturbation analysis and paired ranking comparisons are established; the contribution is a careful adaptation rather than a new estimator.

future_potential.positive: Can distinguish competing failure hypotheses and guide narrowly targeted, jointly trained HSTU changes with documented uncertainty.
future_potential.negative: Frozen-model sensitivity may reflect distribution shift, positional effects, or memorization and has no established relationship to validation improvement.

code_difficulty.positive: Basic fixed-width perturbations and cached-candidate scoring reuse existing hooks without retraining.
code_difficulty.negative: Timestamp alignment, coordinate-preserving masking, repeat-target exclusions, and paired uncertainty require careful implementation; some controls may be unsupported.

related_work.title: Actions Speak Louder than Words: Trillion-Parameter Sequential Transducers for Generative Recommendations
contributions: Introduces HSTU for large-scale sequential recommendation.
Provides the architectural context for gated, non-softmax aggregation and positional/temporal sensitivity.
limitations: Does not establish recent-intent sensitivity for the supplied checkpoint or these four datasets.
Masking, normalization and temporal alignment must be checked against the supplied implementation.

related_work.title: Does It Look Sequential?
contributions: Uses sequence shuffling to investigate sequential structure across recommendation datasets.
Motivates comparing intact and shuffled histories while separating latest-item dependence.
limitations: Order sensitivity cannot identify causal intent or eliminate temporal confounds.
Frozen-model training-prefix sensitivity may reflect memorization rather than transferable dependence.

related_work.title: Betello et al.: Sequential Recommendation Perturbation Analysis
contributions: Studies interaction deletions followed by retraining SASRec and GRU4Rec, including removal of recent interactions.
Introduces Finite Rank-Biased Overlap for comparing finite recommendation lists.
limitations: Does not validate frozen-HSTU inference interventions or their usefulness for selecting improvements.
Ranking stability and recommendation quality are distinct outcomes.

related_work.title: WDC-PAVE
contributions: Distinguishes product-attribute extraction from normalization and evaluates against verified annotations.
limitations: Attribute extraction alone cannot verify user demand or product compatibility.
The proposed local evidence audit requires separate coverage and precision measurements.

related_work.title: Official HSTU implementation
contributions: Provides concrete reference behavior for attention normalization, masking, and relative attention biases.
limitations: Reference behavior must not be assumed to match the host's corrected backbone.
A sequence-only compatibility interface may not expose timestamps or retained coordinates.

related_work.title: Finite Rank-Biased Overlap reference implementation
contributions: Specifies the normalized finite-depth overlap sum used for FRBO.
limitations: Requires explicit depth and persistence parameters.
Measures list stability rather than relevance or accuracy.

related_work.title: A Similarity Measure for Indefinite Rankings
contributions: Introduces rank-biased overlap and its treatment of partially observed rankings.
limitations: Extrapolated RBO is distinct from the normalized finite sum used by FRBO.

related_work.title: Sampled recommendation metric analysis
contributions: Examines limitations of sampled recommendation evaluation, including differences from full-catalog comparisons.
limitations: Fixing candidates reduces paired-comparison noise but does not remove sampling bias.
Does not authorize changing the pinned host evaluation protocol.

related_work.title: SciPy paired bootstrap documentation
contributions: Documents paired resampling and bootstrap interval construction.
limitations: The resampling unit must be adapted to users and category-stratified macro aggregation.
User bootstrap intervals omit checkpoint, training-seed and candidate-sampling uncertainty.
